QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_74

question.text: Jeevan Jyoti Foundation runs a combined Healthcare + Slum-Development programme (mobile clinics INSIDE a slum-rehabilitation zone). This spans SAS-200 and SAS-1100. The SIA's integrated approach should:

answer.text: Prepare a single Social Impact Assessment Report with TWO standard-specific indicator sets, clearly delineated; shared infrastructure (e.g., drinking-water construction) reported once under the primary standard with cross-reference to the secondary
Use SAS-200 only since health is the primary activity
Prepare two completely independent reports with no cross-linkage

explanation.text: **The Logic:** A single integrated Report with standard-specific indicator sections and cross-reference annotations is the cleanest design. Shared infrastructure (water tanks, sanitation) is reported ONCE under the primary standard with cross-reference to avoid double-counting while preserving transparency to Report users. **The Trap:** Option B ignores housing. Option C creates reconciliation nightmares. Option D abandons SIA independence. **Cross-Exam Context:** Integrated-report design logic also in BRSR + SASB combined-framework reporting (III-A / III-C Compliance). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Draft the integrated Report's Contents page as: Section I (shared context), Section II-A (SAS-200 specific), Section II-B (SAS-1100 specific), Section III (joint limitations). Users can navigate by standard or holistically.
